title: All-Inclusive in Crikvenica, Croatia: 2027 Guide
metaDescription: Is there all-inclusive in Crikvenica? Hotel Omorika offers it. Per-person prices, what is included, vs half-board and apartments, and who it suits.
content:
## Does Crikvenica Have All-Inclusive Hotels?

Crikvenica has a limited all-inclusive offer. It is not an all-inclusive resort town in the Turkish or Spanish sense. **Hotel Omorika** is the property that currently lists all-inclusive rates on major booking platforms. It is a three-star hotel on a slope above Omorika beach, with a gravel beach about 100 m away and views toward the island of Krk. A pool complex was added in 2022.

Most other hotels in town sell bed and breakfast or half-board. That includes Hotel Kvarner Palace, Hotel Crikvenica, Hotel Kaštel and Mediteran Maradiso by Aminess. Crikvenica has no large self-contained resort with multiple restaurants and animation programmes.

## What Is Typically Included

Croatian all-inclusive is usually lighter than the Mediterranean resort model. At Omorika, the package covers breakfast, lunch and dinner, plus drinks served with meals. Check the exact hours and the drink list before booking. Local beer, house wine and soft drinks are the usual range. Premium spirits and drinks outside meal times are normally not covered.

Not included: the tourist tax (€2.50 per adult per day in season, €1.50 from October at Kvarner Palace's current tariff), parking, sun loungers on public beaches, spa entry and excursions. Mediteran Maradiso's half-board already includes drinks with dinner in summer, plus pool entry. Its half-board is therefore close to an all-inclusive in practice.

## Price Per Person Per Night: All-Inclusive vs Half-Board vs Apartment

Prices below are rough ranges based on current published tariffs and booking listings. They are per person, assuming two adults sharing a double room.

| Option | Shoulder (May–June, September) | Peak (July–August) |
|---|---|---|
| All-inclusive (Omorika, Lišanj) | ~€80–95 | ~€110–150 |
| Half-board (Mediteran Maradiso) | ~€48–77 | ~€107–141 |
| Half-board (Kvarner Palace, late season) | from €125–150 | higher |
| Apartment, room only (per person, 4 people) | ~€30–40 | ~€45–52 |
| Apartment plus groceries and eating out | ~€60–80 | ~€80–110 |

The all-inclusive figures are estimates. They are anchored on a listed Omorika half-board rate of about €125 for two (roughly €62 per person) and a soft all-inclusive rate of about €184 for two at Aminess Casa Lišanj. A June week at Omorika with all-inclusive has been listed from about €1,800 for the room. Dynamic pricing moves these numbers weekly.

Apartments in Crikvenica average about €149 per night per unit. Peak weeks in July and early August run to about €207 per night for a typical holiday apartment. Late October drops to about €130. A unit sleeping four therefore costs roughly €45–52 per person at peak, before food.

## Who All-Inclusive Suits in Crikvenica

### Families with small children

All-inclusive works well for families with children under 8. Meal times are fixed, buffets handle fussy eaters, and nobody has to cook after a beach day. A hotel with a pool, such as Omorika, removes the pebble-beach problem. Crikvenica's central beaches are gravel, and Kvarner Palace's nearby beach is sandy. Children often pay little or nothing when sharing a room with two adults, which improves the per-person maths.

### Short stays of 2–4 nights

Short stays favour hotel board. There is no time to shop, and apartments often require a minimum of 5–7 nights in July and August. For a long weekend, half-board at a hotel is usually the better deal. All-inclusive adds little when drinks are mostly water and one beer.

### Who should self-cater

Groups of three or more, stays of 7+ nights, and travellers who like to eat out are better off in an apartment. Crikvenica's promenade has a good choice of konobas and pizzerias, and a market sells fresh fruit and fish. A family of four in a €180 apartment pays about €45 per person for the room, then spends less on food than the all-inclusive premium. Peak all-inclusive for four adults can pass €500 per night.

Skip all-inclusive in Crikvenica if you want to explore. Buying lunch and dinner you will not eat, because you are in Selce, on Krk or at a Rijeka sight, wastes money. Half-board is the better compromise for most couples.

## Nearest All-Inclusive Options

The closest alternative is in neighbouring Novi Vinodolski, about 10 km south. Aminess Casa Lišanj, a three-star hotel there, sells soft all-inclusive with gravel beach under 50 m away. The wider Kvarner coast has more all-inclusive hotels. Opatija and Rabac, and Krk island resorts such as Punat, carry larger Valamar and Falkensteiner offers. Rijeka is about 30 minutes by car from Crikvenica and is the usual transfer point.

## Insider Tips

- Book half-board with drinks at dinner, as at Mediteran Maradiso, before paying for full all-inclusive. The price gap is often larger than the extra value.
- Late September to early November is cheaper. Kvarner Palace ran stay-7-pay-6 offers from mid-September to 8 November 2026. Check whether a similar offer runs in 2027.
- Ask the hotel which meals the all-inclusive covers. Packages differ on lunch, snacks and bar hours.
- Hotel parking can be costly. Hotel Crikvenica charges €17 per day for parking 800 m from the hotel, which affects the total.

## FAQ

See the FAQ section below for quick answers.

faq.question: Is there an all-inclusive hotel in Crikvenica?
faq.answer: Yes. Hotel Omorika offers all-inclusive rates, covering three meals and drinks served with meals. It is the main option in town. Most other hotels sell breakfast or half-board only.

faq.question: How much is all-inclusive per person per night in Crikvenica?
faq.answer: Roughly €80–95 in shoulder season and €110–150 in July and August, based on current hotel and booking rates. Prices change weekly, so these are estimates. Children sharing a room often pay a reduced rate.

faq.question: Is half-board cheaper than all-inclusive in Crikvenica?
faq.answer: Usually, yes. Mediteran Maradiso's half-board runs from €48 per person in spring and autumn to about €107–141 in peak weeks, with drinks at dinner included in summer. Kvarner Palace half-board starts around €125–150 per person in late season.

faq.question: Is an apartment cheaper than all-inclusive in Crikvenica?
faq.answer: For three or more people, mostly yes. The average apartment costs about €149 per night per unit, around €180–207 in peak weeks. With groceries and some meals out, a family of four typically pays less than all-inclusive.

faq.question: Where is the nearest all-inclusive resort to Crikvenica?
faq.answer: Aminess Casa Lišanj in Novi Vinodolski, about 10 km south, offers soft all-inclusive. Larger all-inclusive resorts are in Opatija, Rabac and on Krk island. Rijeka is about 30 minutes away by car.

faq.question: Is all-inclusive worth it for a family with small children?
faq.answer: Yes, for stays of about a week with children under 8. Fixed meals, pool access and no cooking make days easier. For older children or travellers who want to eat out, half-board or an apartment gives better value.

quickAnswer: Yes, but the choice is small. Hotel Omorika is the one Crikvenica hotel that currently sells all-inclusive board. Expect roughly €80–95 per person per night in shoulder season and €110–150 in July–August. Half-board costs less, and apartments with self-catering are cheapest for groups of three or more.
